content.content:
1	# Issue #230 — a web control surface on the remote port: investigation notes
2	
3	Read: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/design.md` (headings, "Remote client (2026-10-12)" at line 3107, "Trust boundary" at 219 skimmed by heading only), `docs/lessons.md`, `docs/remote-client.md` (§0–§5, §6, §9; §10–§13 only by heading). Line numbers are as in this worktree (HEAD 7fe8949, Release 0.4.1). No code was run, nothing was built.
4	
5	## 1. What is on disk, and how it rehydrates (before any pane)
6	
7	A browser control surface adds no new durable record by itself; the existing remote records carry it.
8	
9	- `identity.json` (`src/ports/remote.rs:26` `Identity`): server id, display name, certificate DER (public), `spki_sha256`, `listen {lan, port}`. Private key in the Keychain under `remote-key:<server_id>`. The page needs nothing new here. A browser pins nothing, so the certificate and key hash are the only host-identity facts the page can use.
10	- `devices.json` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96` `PairedDevice`): `id, name, scope, token_sha256, created, last_seen`. A browser is one more row. The issue's decision 6 ("name from the user agent") needs **no schema change**: `/pair` already takes `device_name` (`src/app.rs:3650`), so the page can send the name it derives. If the host should derive it from the `User-Agent` header, `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444`) keeps no such header today, so `RemoteRequest` (`:360`) would need an additive field. That is not a `model.rs` type, so no `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump. Adding a "kind" field to `PairedDevice` is serde-default-able but is a contract extension to decide on.
11	- The pairing window is in core state only, never saved (`src/core/action.rs:978` `PairingWindow {until, code, scope, failures}`; `PAIRING_WINDOW` 5 min, `PAIRING_ATTEMPTS` 3). Restart loses it, as the spec intends.
12	- **Rehydration of the browser's session is the browser's, not the host's.** The host rehydrates a device purely from `token_sha256` → `PairedDevice` (`core.device_by_token`, used in `authenticate`, `src/app.rs:3114`). So whichever way the token reaches requests (header, cookie, subprotocol), the host-side check is the same hash lookup, and revoking the row (`AppAction::RevokeDevice`, `src/core/remote.rs:86`) kills it on the next request. `dispatch_inner` (`src/app.rs:486`) already drops that device's subscribers, which closes its WebSocket. The page does not need to learn the old state to recover: it needs a stable way to tell "401, revoked or unknown token" from "key changed" from "host unreachable".
13	- What the page keeps on the device (token, or a cookie, plus the server's key hash and id) is the one new storage decision. It lives outside the tree; see Open questions.
14	- Live state is a cache, as the repo's idea says: the page's view is rebuilt from `GET /api/v1/projects`, `/projects/{id}/sessions`, `/waiting`, then the `/events` `hello {epoch, revision}`, with snapshot-after-subscribe and revision-held-per-key (§4.2, §4.4). A changed `epoch` means refetch everything.
15	
16	## 2. The code the issue touches (files and lines in this tree)
17	
18	Host listener, `src/adapters/remote.rs` (1088 lines)
19	- `read_request` `:444`. Parses method, target, lowercased headers; keeps only `content-length`, `authorization: Bearer`, and `upgrade`+`sec-websocket-key`. It does not keep `Cookie`, `Origin`, `Host`, `User-Agent`, `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` or `If-None-Match`. MAX_HEAD / MAX_BODY bound it. The query is kept undecoded as pairs (`:495`), documented as "ids and numbers only".
20	- `respond` `:530`. Always `Content-Type: application/json`, `Connection: keep-alive`, no other header. There is no way today to set `Content-Type: text/html`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `Cache-Control`, `Set-Cookie`, or `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` on the 101 (`respond_upgrade` `:519`). Statuses with reasons are a fixed list (`200 400 401 403 404 405 413 429 503 504`); a 304 or 301 would print "Error".
21	- `respond_upgrade` `:519` does not echo a subprotocol and does not check `Origin`.
22	- Pools and rate windows `:570–640`: `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED = 4`, `MAX_PAIRED = 12`, `PAIR_PER_MINUTE = 6`, `INFO_PER_MINUTE = 60`. `Limits::limited(path)` (`:631`) matches only the exact `PAIR_PATH`/`INFO_PATH`, so any other path, including `/`, is unlimited by rate. A connection is "unauthenticated" until the frame answers one request with `authenticated: true` (`connection`, `:770`, moves it to the paired pool then). A browser's first page load, `/info`, `/pair`, each on a keep-alive connection, sits in the 4-slot pool; browsers also open several parallel connections for a page with a few files (not measured).
23	- `connection` `:770`: TLS handshake, then one request at a time to the frame via `shared.requests.try_send`; a full channel answers 503.
24	- `local_address` `:962`: the one routed address, as the QR's `addresses`. `make_identity` `:95`: the certificate is built with `CertificateParams::new(Vec::new())`, so **no Subject Alternative Name** and CN `Switchboard <server_id>`; the key is P-256 ECDSA, validity "year 4096". Native clients never look at name or validity (the `Pin` verifier `:183`); a browser does.
25	
26	Frame, `src/app.rs` (4482 lines)
27	- `serve_pending` `:1572` drains the port (`DRAIN_PER_PASS` 8) and calls `serve_remote`.
28	- `serve_remote` `:3017`. First line: `request.path.strip_prefix("/api/v1/")`; anything else → `refuse(..., 404, "not_found", ..., false)`. `GET /` therefore answers a JSON 404 today. `("GET", ["info"])` and `("POST", ["pair"])` are served before `authenticate`. Everything else goes through `authenticate` (`:3103`), which reads **only `request.bearer`**. Then `("GET", ["events"])` → `remote_subscribe` (`:2723`), and the allowlist `match` of reads/commands. Commands need `Scope::Control` (`remote_command`, `:~3170`, a read device gets 403 `scope`).
29	- `remote_info` `:3567`: server id and name, protocol, capabilities, `spki_sha256`, version, limits, `pairing_open`. Served to anyone, so the page's "compare the URL's `key` with what `/info` presents" works with an existing endpoint. Note, though: the page script cannot read the certificate or its key from `fetch`, only `/info`'s JSON claim of the key. If the host is an impostor, it will say whatever it likes (this is the issue's own caveat; see Open questions).
30	- `remote_pair` `:3606`. Requires an open window; requires `spki_sha256` in the body to equal the identity's, else `PairingFailed` (counts toward the three) and 403 `wrong_key`; code compared uppercased; token 32 random bytes base64url; reply `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}` in an envelope, `authenticated: false`. The token is in the JSON body, so the reply cannot be the cookie-setting one without `respond` gaining headers.
31	- `remote_subscribe` `:2723`; `subscriber_frame` `:1704` handles `watch`/`unwatch` text frames, so the page gets `screen` and `conversation` `changed` events only by sending `watch` for those keys, as §4.4 says.
32	- Content routes: `last-response`, `screen`, `conversation` at `:1967` (`ContentView::LastResponse`), `remote_content_route`; dispatched through the content worker.
33	- `serve_remote` match, and the existing test of the allowlist, `tests/remote.rs:682`, both treat any non-`/api/v1/` path as "not available". The issue's "any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" is a code fact at `:3023`.
34	
35	Pairing window UI, `src/ui/remote.rs` (317 lines)
36	- `pairing` `:141`: the QR payload is built at `:160` as `serde_json::json!({server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses})`. Address is `remote::local_address()` + `cx.remote_port.unwrap_or(identity.listen.port)`. `Copy invite` (`:~207`) copies the same JSON text. `qr_texture` `:280`. The dialog's devices table is `devices` `:230` (name, scope combo, paired, seen, Revoke). The scope radio and "Allow pairing for 5 minutes" is `:218–228`.
37	- `host` `:89`: the LAN checkbox hover says "only paired devices get past /info". The issue's amended wording ("`/info`, `/pair` and now the page itself") would change this sentence and the §5 rule.
38	- The QR is built only when the window opens; it needs the port and the address, which are UI-side today (`cx.remote_port`). A URL needs the host form. For an IPv6 or a `.local` name the URL form differs; the code uses one IPv4 address from `local_address()`, with `0.0.0.0` bind when `listen.lan`.
39	- When `listen.lan` is false (loopback), `local_address()` still gives the LAN IP in the QR; that address will not answer. Whether the pairing window should say so is an existing gap, and it matters more with a phone (see Open questions).
40	
41	Core, `src/core/remote.rs` (176 lines): `remote_action` `:21`, `identity` `:127`, `pairing_at` `:152` (time-gated), `new_device` `:166`. A page does not change core.
42	
43	Swift side
44	- `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift`: `PairingInvite` (the JSON `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`) with `parse(_ text:)` decoding JSON only; a URL string fails with a decoding error. Callers: `client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift:107` (one-arg form, plus a three-arg form `host:port code spki`), `client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:106` (dev invite) and `:883` (the headset's paste field), `ConnectionManager.pair(invite:)` `:482` (uses `invite.addresses.compactMap(Address.init).first`). Tests for it are in `client/Tests/SwitchboardProtocolTests/FixturesTests.swift` and `SwitchboardClientCoreTests`. Nothing in these has been run.
45	- `client/Fixtures` is written by `tests/remote.rs::write_fixtures` `:1587` and read by the Swift tests; the issue says extend if a view changes. A URL invite would be a new fixture line if the parser is changed.
46	
47	Tests, `tests/remote.rs` (3592 lines)
48	- Harness: a real TLS listener with fakes; `Port` `:37`, `http()` `:245` (a hand-written HTTP/1.1 client over `pinned_client`, writes only `Authorization: Bearer`, reads headers only for `Content-Length`), `call()` `:299` (drives `serve_pending` on the test thread while a client thread talks), `pair()` `:406`, `subscribe()` `:1955`. Existing relevant tests: `info_is_served_to_anyone_and_every_other_read_is_refused_unpaired` `:426` (asserts `/other` → 404 JSON `not_found`; this changes when `GET /` serves HTML only if `/other` stays as is), the allowlist test `:682`, `pair_is_rate_limited_per_listener` `:1406`, `stalled_strangers_fill_their_own_pool...` `:3226`, `revoke_closes_the_devices_socket` `:2892`, `the_client_fixtures_decode_on_both_sides` `:1829`.
49	- `http()` discards response headers, so a header assertion (Content-Type, CSP, Cache-Control) needs a helper that returns them; no such helper exists.
50	- No test drives a browser, and CLAUDE.md says UI tests (`tests/ui.rs`) are egui-only, so the page's JavaScript has no test tooling in the tree. There is no `web/` directory and no `include_str!` of text assets (`include_bytes!` only for fonts and the icon, `src/main.rs:167`, `src/ui/theme.rs:203`).
51	
52	Not on the wire: **the card's one-line excerpt.** `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637`) has `card` (the state word), `waiting`, `waiting_reason`, `last_stop_at_ms`, `quiet_secs`, `pending`, `trust_question`, and no excerpt. The card's excerpt is computed in `src/ui/cards.rs:558` `agent_excerpt` from the parsed conversation (first line of the last turn's `final_text`, else the last activity, else `You: <prompt>`, 160 chars), and for non-agent sessions from `UiState.captions` (`cards.rs:177–182`), which the core never reads. So "each with its kind, state and the one-line excerpt the card shows" cannot be produced from the list reads alone. Either the page fetches `/last-response` per listed session (N content reads, each through the one content worker, each entering the watch set `WATCH_CAP` 128) and cuts the first line itself, or the read model gains a field. The issue says "no new read model unless the page cannot do without one"; this is the one place it may. The excerpt logic is in `ui/`, which CLAUDE.md says should move to the core if reused.
53	
54	Docs that the plan amends
55	- `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1 (bounds: 16 conn, 4 unauth, 6 `/pair` and 60 `/info` per minute), §4.2, §4.3 (table: add `GET /` and the page's paths, or a separate "page" section), §4.4, §5 (pairing; "Require pairing before anything but `/info` and `/pair`"; "The token ... only as a bearer header over the pinned connection, never in a URL"; QR contents), §9. Also the "Remote client (2026-10-12)" status section in `docs/design.md:3107` and its end-of-section text, `README.md` Layout table (`:369–446`; new `web/` and any new file), `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased line, and the pairing dialog text.
56	- §5 says the QR carries JSON and "A client without a camera ... pairs from the host's Bonjour record"; it also says a client "scans or types both". The URL form changes both lines.
57	
58	## 3. How the surfaces would sit (shape, then pane)
59	
60	1. Adapter: serve static files before the frame. Two options in the tree's idiom: (a) answer them on the connection thread from `&'static str`s (no frame, no `RemoteIncoming`), which keeps them off the 8-per-pass drain and out of the frame, but then they need their own rate/pool rule because `Limits::limited` and the unauthenticated pool apply by path; or (b) hand them to `serve_remote` as a `Served::Now` like `/info`, with `respond` taking a content type and extra headers. CLAUDE.md puts "what the frame decides" in `app.rs`, "moves bytes and enforces bounds that need no state" in the adapter, which points at (a) for constant files, but a decision about `Set-Cookie` after `/pair` is frame state, so `RemoteReply` would need additive header fields in either case.
61	2. Auth carrier: `authenticate` reads `request.bearer` only. A cookie or a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` carrier means `read_request` keeps another header and `RemoteRequest` gains a field (additive; the file's types are adapter-local, not `model.rs`/`action.rs`). The 101 reply would have to echo the chosen subprotocol if that route is picked, or a conforming browser closes the socket.
62	3. Page: `web/` with `index.html`, a script, a stylesheet, embedded by `include_str!` (new in the tree), constants in the adapter or a small `src/web.rs`. The first cut's views map to endpoints already in the allowlist: `/projects`, `/projects/{id}/sessions`, `/waiting`, `/sessions/{id}/last-response`, `/sessions/{id}/screen`, `POST /sessions/{id}/send`, `/events`, `/info`, `/pair`.
63	4. Pairing window: the URL instead of (or beside) the JSON; the CLI and headset text paths must accept both.
64	
65	## 4. Things found that bear on the decisions
66	
67	- Decision 4's "which pool and rate window": today there is none for static paths; `Limits::limited` ignores them and the connection counts as unauthenticated until a paired request. A page load does not reach the frame under (a), so the 4-slot unauthenticated pool is the only bound, and a phone page loading three files over three connections can occupy most of it while the owner's other devices are unaffected (they have the paired pool). Not measured.
68	- `GET /` is currently a JSON 404 through `refuse`, which logs by path and code (`src/app.rs:3754`). A stranger probing `/` with a browser thus gets a JSON error today.
69	- The WebSocket handshake checks neither `Origin` nor `Host`, and `authenticate` is a pure bearer check. Today that is safe because a bearer header cannot be sent by a cross-site page. A cookie carrier changes that: a cookie rides on any request the browser makes to that origin, so the cross-site-request and cross-site-WebSocket cases need an `Origin` check on `POST` and on the upgrade in addition to `SameSite=Strict`. The page is same-origin, but a hostile page on another host-name for the same IP is a different origin that a browser would still send `SameSite=Strict` cookies to only when same-site; `SameSite` is by registrable domain and ignores port, so another service on the same IP and another port is same-site. That is a claim about browsers, not settled here.
70	- The token in a `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value is visible to the script (it must put it there), so it lives in script-readable storage; the cookie route keeps it away from script but ties the carrier to the browser's cookie rules for a self-signed origin (see Open questions).
71	- The pairing `/pair` reply is `authenticated: false`, so after pairing, the first authenticated request moves the connection to the paired pool; the page's keep-alive connection does the same. No change needed.
72	- `query` is stored undecoded and documented "ids and numbers only". The page's own `?code=&key=&id=` is read client-side and never sent to the host except in the initial `GET /?code=...` request itself: the **request line carries the code to the host and into whatever logs it**. `refuse` logs "by method, path and code only", `read_request` splits the query off, and the connection thread does not log. Still, the code is in the browser's history and any proxy or `Referer` until `replaceState` runs, and in the QR. The issue's `history.replaceState` handles the address bar; a page-load request to `/?code=...` has already been made, so the code has been sent to the host in the clear of nothing but TLS. That is acceptable only because the host is the one that issued it. It is not hidden from an impostor host; this is the issue's own trust-step caveat.
73	- The code is single-use and closes the window on success (§5), and three wrong codes close it. A QR URL opened twice (a link preview, a camera app prefetching, a messaging app unfurling a pasted URL) is a `GET` only, not a `/pair`, so it does not consume the code. A **link previewer's own GET** hits the host with no cookies; it would be served the page. Not a code use, but see the open question on prefetch.
74	- Existing text path for the CLI: `switchboard-remote pair '<invite json>'` via `PairingInvite.parse`. A URL would need a parser that accepts `https://host:port/?code&key&id`. `addresses` is a `[String]` of `host:port`; a URL has one authority. 1	# Facts for issue #230 (web control surface)
2	
3	No spike was run. Every open question is either answered by a source or needs a device, so no experiment here could settle it. The worktree has no changes.
4	
5	## Settled
6	
7	- The certificate has no Subject Alternative Name and its CN is `Switchboard <server_id>`. Evidence: `src/adapters/remote.rs:102` (`CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())`), `:91` (not_after "year 4096").
8	- Apple platforms do not trust a DNS name that appears only in the CommonName. They want the name in the SAN, `serverAuth` EKU, and validity of 825 days or fewer for certificates issued after 2019-07-01. The current certificate fails all three, so Safari may refuse it outright instead of showing a clickable warning. Evidence: https://support.apple.com/en-us/103769. Whether Safari offers "Visit this website" for it is Unresolved.
9	- A bare IP in the URL needs an IP-type SAN to match, and the certificate has none. The Apple page speaks only of DNS names, so this half is inference. Evidence: none beyond the rows above (see Unresolved).
10	- `new WebSocket(url, protocols)` takes no headers. A token can travel only in the URL, in a cookie, or in the subprotocol list. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket/WebSocket.
11	- Subprotocol carrier, RFC 6455:
12	  - Values must be tokens (U+0021–U+007E minus separators). Base64url fits.
13	  - If the client sends the header and the server omits it from the 101 reply, the browser fails the connection. The server must echo exactly one of the values.
14	  - Browsers must send `Origin` on the upgrade. Checking it is optional for the server, and without a check the server accepts connections from anywhere.
15	  - Evidence: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6455 §1.9, §4.1, §4.2.2.
16	- `respond_upgrade` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:519`) echoes no subprotocol and checks no `Origin`. `read_request` (`:444`) keeps only `content-length`, bearer, and the upgrade key. Both would need additive changes for either carrier.
17	- Cookie attributes:
18	  - `HttpOnly` hides the cookie from script, but the browser still sends it on `fetch` calls.
19	  - `Secure` cookies are sent only over `https:`.
20	  - `SameSite=Strict` is relative to the *site*, which is scheme plus eTLD+1 with the port ignored. Another service on the same IP at another port is same-site, so a cookie token needs a server-side `Origin` check on the upgrade and on `POST`.
21	  - Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Set-Cookie; https://web.dev/articles/same-site-same-origin.
22	- CSP `connect-src 'self'` does not cover `ws:`/`wss:` in all browsers. The plan should name `wss://<origin>` or `wss:` explicitly. Evidence: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/connect-src, which cites w3c/webappsec-csp#7.
23	- `respond` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:530`) always sends `Content-Type: application/json` and no other header, and the status reasons are a fixed list. Serving HTML needs content type, CSP, cache and cookie headers added to `RemoteReply`. Only `src/adapters/remote.rs:360/506` and `src/app.rs` (about 20 sites) construct `RemoteReply`. `RemoteRequest` is built only at `src/adapters/remote.rs:506`, so adding a field there breaks no test or fake literal. Evidence: grep `RemoteRequest {` and `RemoteReply {` over `src` and `tests`.
24	- `Limits::limited` rate-limits only the exact `/pair` and `/info` paths. A page load counts against no rate window, only the 4-slot unauthenticated pool. Evidence: `src/adapters/remote.rs:631`; `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1.
25	- `serve_remote` (`src/app.rs:3017–3023`) refuses any path outside `/api/v1/` with a JSON 404. The tests that assert this are `tests/remote.rs:426/462` (`/other`) and `:682`. They stay valid if `/other` is still refused.
26	- The card's one-line excerpt is not on the wire. `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637`) has no excerpt. `agent_excerpt` is in `src/ui/cards.rs:558`, and shell captions are `UiState` only (`cards.rs:177–182`). `last-response` (`GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}/last-response`, `docs/remote-client.md:173`) goes through the single content worker, `ContentKey::Conversation` (`src/app.rs:1967`). Each viewed key joins the watch set (cap 128, from the investigation's `WATCH_CAP` note). The plan must choose: N content reads, or an additive `SessionView` field computed in the core.
27	- No tree document says anything about a browser surface, a cookie, or certificate download. `grep` for browser/cookie/origin over `docs/remote-client.md`, `docs/design.md` and `spikes/22-remote-port/README.md` finds only "browser" meaning the native app's session browser.
28	- Swift `PairingInvite.parse` decodes JSON only (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift`). The call sites are `client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift:107` and `client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:106/883`. A URL form needs a parser branch and a new fixture line in `tests/remote.rs::write_fixtures` (`:1587`).
29	- `cx.remote_port` comes from `app.remote_addr()` (`src/ui/mod.rs:420`) and falls back to `identity.listen.port`. The QR address is `local_address()` even when `listen.lan` is false, so the phone would be handed an address that does not answer. This is an existing gap that the plan should close (warn, or require LAN on).
30	- Build: root `Cargo.toml:91` excludes only `vendor/egui_term`, and `include_str!("../web/...")` from a root-level directory needs no packaging change. CI is a single `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. No script lists a file set (`grep` of `scripts/bundle.sh`, `ci.yml`, `Cargo.toml` found none), though `scripts/release.sh` was not read.
31	
32	## Unresolved
33	
34	- Whether Safari (iOS/iPadOS/macOS), Chrome, Firefox and Android Chrome allow a click-through for this certificate (no SAN, CN-only, year-4096 expiry, opened by bare IPv4). Tried: Apple's requirements page (above), which says the certificate fails and "can break ... Safari page loads". Chrome's CN-fallback removal could not be confirmed, because chromestatus returned no text. Needs a device. If the click-through is a hard error, decision 1 is forced: the host must put the IP in a SAN, or serve a downloadable certificate.
35	- Whether `fetch`, `wss://`, and a `Secure` cookie keep working after a click-through, per browser and for how long. No primary source found. Needs a device.
36	- iOS certificate-profile install for a self-signed leaf with no CA bit: whether it is accepted and then trusted under Certificate Trust Settings. Tried only the Apple server-requirements page, which does not cover profiles. Not settled.
37	- Whether the iOS camera opens `https://<ipv4>:<port>/?code=…&key=<64 hex>&id=<uuid>` (about 140 characters) as a link, and whether the camera or a link previewer fetches the URL before the owner taps. No source found. Needs a phone.
38	- Whether `history.replaceState` keeps the code out of Safari's history and recents. No source found. Needs a phone.
39	- `User-Agent` naming: iPadOS Safari reports a desktop Mac by default. No source fetched. Needs a device.
40	- Whether the Safari/iOS WebSocket reconnects after sleep, and how it behaves after a certificate exception. Not found.
41	- Parallel-connection behaviour of a phone against the 4-slot unauthenticated pool. Needs a running host and a phone (not run here).
42	- Browser URL rules for IPv6 literals, link-local zones and `.local`. Not fetched. `local_address()` currently returns one IPv4.
43	- Whether `Cache-Control`/`Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`/`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` suffice for a URL that carried a code. Standard practice and no primary source fetched. The plan can adopt them, but they are unverified.
44	- How a later visit learns its scope. The `/pair` reply carries `scope`, but the cookie holds only the token, and there is no `/me`. The plan can read the scope from the `/pair` reply and remember it, or add an additive field. This is a design choice, not a world fact.
45	
46	## For the owner
47	
48	- **Certificate trust.** Does the owner accept a click-through warning on the local network as the trust step (said in the paired-devices dialog), or want a downloadable certificate?
49	  - If click-through and the target browsers refuse a no-SAN certificate: the plan must reissue the certificate with the IP and `serverAuth` in a SAN and validity of 825 days or fewer. This changes the SPKI only if the key changes. A re-pin with a new certificate on the same key keeps the pin, but the plan must check `identity.json` migration.
50	  - If download: the plan adds a certificate route and dialog text. A profile-install flow has to be tried on a device first.
51	- **Token carrier.** The plan should pick based on the answer.
52	  - Cookie (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict`): the script never sees the token, but the host must check `Origin` on the upgrade and on `POST` and needs a `Set-Cookie` header on the `/pair` reply.
53	  - Subprotocol: needs the 101 echo, and the token sits in script-readable storage.
54	- **One URL or JSON too.** May the QR's JSON be dropped? If yes, the CLI and headset parsers take the URL only, and the fixtures change. If no, parsers accept both and the QR is the URL.
55	- **Excerpt on the wire.** May `SessionView` gain an additive excerpt field? If yes, compute it in the core (moving `agent_excerpt`). If no, the page fetches `last-response` per visible session, bounded by the worker and the watch cap.
56	- **Devices for acceptance.** Does the owner have a phone, an iPad and a signed bundle on the LAN? If not, the acceptance steps (scan, warning, waiting rises, reply, revoke) are not verifiable and tests must stand in with the host's own HTTP client.
57	- **Browser device name.** What should an iPad (which reports as a Mac) be called? If the page may edit the name before pairing, `/pair` already takes `device_name`, and no schema change is needed. If the host derives it from `User-Agent`, `RemoteRequest` gains an additive field.

### 4.1 Implementation

- **No Tokio.** The host is std threads and `mpsc`; the core is owned by `SwitchboardApp` and every state change is a dispatch on the frame thread. The remote port follows the `ControlSocket` shape: an accept thread per listener, one thread per connection, each request handed over a channel to the frame, answered by the same `serve` path in `app.rs` (`serve_pending` runs before every frame, hidden ones included), the reply sent back on the connection's channel. A second runtime inside an egui app buys nothing for a handful of connections.
- **The frame does core state only.** A metadata request (a view, a command) is answered on the frame as the control port is. A content request (conversation, screen, run output, file) takes two steps: the frame answers with the **handle and the redaction policy** (the transcript path and resume handle, the pane's host id, the run's log path, the file's root and relative path, plus the secret values to mask and the policy fingerprint), and one **content worker thread** does the read, the parse, the mask, the version check and the serialization from a queue of such requests (one at a time, so one large parse is in memory at once; Spike 22 measured 575 MB peak for the largest transcript), then sends one small action back to the frame to record the version it observed (§4.4), and the connection thread writes the reply. The watch poll (§4.4) runs through the same worker. A multi-megabyte transcript, a 768 KiB file or a slow Keychain call therefore costs the worker its time and the asking connection its wait, never a frame. The handle is read under the frame's authority, so a record removed or rebound between the two steps makes the worker's version action a no-op and the reply carries the handle it read from.
- **Bounds.** The port is one user's few devices, and the limits say so:
  - at most 16 connections in total and 4 unauthenticated ones; a further accept is closed at once. The 4 are a separate pool: an unauthenticated flood fills its own slots and never a paired client's;
  - `/pair` is answered at most six times a minute per listener and `/info` sixty; past that the connection thread answers 429 without reaching the frame;
  - a TLS handshake and the first request line each within 5 s, a request body within 10 s, a write within 10 s; a connection that misses a deadline is closed;
  - one request in flight per connection (HTTP/1.1, no pipelining);
  - the frame drains at most 8 remote requests per pass, in arrival order, the rest waiting on the channel; the channel is bounded at 64 and a full channel answers 503 from the connection thread without reaching the frame; a frame-side request is a view or a handle lookup and takes microseconds, so the count is the bound;
  - each WebSocket subscriber has an event queue of 256; when it fills, the subscriber is sent `resync_required` and closed, never silently trimmed (§4.4);
  - the watch set (§4.4) is capped at 128 keys for the whole port; past the cap the least recently read key is evicted silently, since a read of an evicted key always works and re-enters it.
- Preferred crates: a blocking HTTP/1.1 server over `std::net::TcpListener` (hand-rolled or `tiny_http`), `tungstenite` for WebSocket, `rustls` with `rcgen` for the per-installation certificate, and `mdns-sd` (or the system `dns-sd` through a small macOS adapter) for Bonjour. All of it in `src/adapters/remote.rs` behind a `ports::remote` trait with a fake, and all of it must compile on Linux CI (Bonjour may be a `cfg(target_os = "macos")` adapter with a no-op elsewhere). **Spike 22 (§10) decides the exact crates before any of this is built.**
- Handlers are thin: HTTP request → auth and scope check → allowlist → `wire::Request` → `serve` → redaction → `wire::Reply` → HTTP response. No session or transcript logic lives in the adapter.
- Only the instance holding the store lock listens (as the control port does); a read-only instance refuses to bind.
- Bind to loopback by default until remote access is explicitly enabled in Settings. For LAN access, bind the chosen interface and require pairing.
- Configurable port in `identity.json` (§3.1), default `43187`, overridable with `SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE_PORT` (a dev aid, documented in the README) so two instances can run on one machine; `0` picks a free one, which the tests use.
- Advertise `_switchboard._tcp` via Bonjour only while listening on a non-loopback interface. TXT records carry the protocol major version (`v`), the display name (`name`) and the `server_id` (`id`, so a client matches a record to a known server before it connects); never a token, never key material. The instance name is the display name with a short id suffix, so two installations on one machine stay distinct.
- If Switchboard closes, the port goes away. A standalone daemon is not in scope.

### 4.2 API conventions
### 4.3 Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Wire body | Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/v1/info` | new: `info` | none (identity only, before pairing) |
| POST | `/api/v1/pair` | pairing handshake (§5) | none, only inside the pairing window |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects` | `projects`; `?scope=all` includes Dispatch's worker records | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/spaces` | `spaces` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/spaces/{id}/sets` | `sets` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sets/{id}` | new: `set` (the `SetView` with pins) | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{id}/sessions` | `sessions`; `?scope=all` as above | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}` | `session` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/waiting` | `waiting`; `?scope=all` as above | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/screen?lines=n` | `session.screen` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation?from=turn\|last&limit=n`, or `?before=turn&limit=n` | new: `session.conversation` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/conversation/{n}` | new: `session.turn` (one turn with its activity uncut) | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/last-response` | new: `session.last_response` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/runs` | new: `session.runs` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/runs/{n}/output?lines=n` | new: `session.run_output` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/projects/{id}/files/{path}` | new: `file.read` (pinned files only) | read |
| POST | `/api/v1/projects/{id}/sessions` | `session.new` (§4.5) | control |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/send` | `session.send` | control |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/resume` | `session.resume` | control |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/trust` | `session.trust` | control |
| GET | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/draft` | `session.draft` | read |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/draft` | `session.draft` | control |
| POST | `/api/v1/sessions/{id}/dictation` | `session.dictation` | control |
| GET | `/api/v1/ops/{op}` | `op.status` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/dispatch/tickets` | new: the core's `TicketListing` (§4.7) | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/dispatch/tickets/{id}` | new: `TicketDetail` | read |
| POST | `/api/v1/dispatch/tickets/{id}/decide` | new: the Mac's `DispatchDecide` | control |
| POST | `/api/v1/dispatch/tickets/{id}/resume` | new: the Mac's `DispatchResume` | control |
| POST | `/api/v1/dispatch/tickets/{id}/close` | new: the Mac's `DispatchClose` | control |
| GET | `/api/v1/dispatch/tickets/{id}/files/{key}` | new: the Mac's `DispatchReadArtifact`, or the disk for an image | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/dispatch/tickets/{id}/events` | new: the Mac's `DispatchReadEvents` | read |
| GET | `/api/v1/events` | WebSocket upgrade | read |

Everything else on the wire is **refused before translation**, by an allowlist, not a denylist: `env.resolve` returns secret values; the `env.*` writes, `definition.install`, `project.add`, `project.root`, `set.sync`, `workflow.*`, `dispatch.runner`, `session.kill` and `session.remove` change what runs on the host or what it keeps. v1 remote is the table above and nothing more.

**Redaction, one policy for every text that leaves the port, applied before any cut.** `session.screen` today masks the values of the project's secret variables and of the session's granted environment sets, and it reads slack lines above the window first so a value wrapped across the window's first line is still found whole. The port generalizes both halves of that: one `redact` function in `app.rs`, and the rule that **masking runs over complete source text, and every cut comes after**, since a value split by a cut no longer matches. Per kind:
  - **conversation**: the parser caps tool detail at `DETAIL_CAP` while parsing, so masking a parsed turn would miss a value crossing that cap. The transcript reader gains an additive `read_masked(handle, &dyn Fn(&str) -> String)` that applies the mask to every string field before `cap`; the port's conversation cache (§4.4) is populated through it, keyed by the secret set's fingerprint as well, and is separate from the UI's unmasked cache. The 256 KiB turn cut then runs on masked text.
  - **run output**: `scrollback::tail_text` cuts bytes before stripping escapes and choosing lines. It gains an overlap: the read starts `longest secret length` bytes before the tail window, the mask runs over the whole buffer, and the line selection then discards the overlap; a value straddling the window's first byte is therefore masked whole. A secret value containing a newline is masked only within a line, which the dialog's sentence on redaction covers.
  - **screen**: the existing slack-lines read, unchanged.
  - **file content**: the file is read whole under its limit, masked, then sent.
  - **last response** and the card excerpt: masked from the turn's full text, then cut.
  The secret set for a session is the project's secret variables plus its granted sets; for a file it is the owning project's. The set is resolved **before any cached content is returned**, on every read, and its **policy fingerprint** (a hash over the sorted names and values, held in memory only, never logged or stored) is part of every masked cache's version (§4.4): a new grant, a changed value or a removed set makes previously masked bytes stale even when their source did not move. If the secret set cannot be resolved (a Keychain error, a missing set), the reply is **refused** with that reason, never sent unredacted and never served from a cached success. What this covers is exactly the values Switchboard holds: a secret the user pasted into a prompt, or one a tool printed that Switchboard never knew, is not found. The paired-devices dialog says this in a sentence, and the claim in design.md's trust boundary is widened to "or as redacted text on the remote port".

New read models, added to the wire crate:

- `session.conversation`: the `Conversation` from `ports::transcript` as a wire shape: title, model, branch, usage, and turns paged by **turn number** (`n`, 1-based). The host parses the whole JSONL, as the session view does, from the app-level cache (§4.4); a transcript the app can show is one the port can serve, and the supported size is whatever the app handles, which the spike measures. What paging bounds is the **response**: a page anchored at its start (`from=turn`) stops at `limit` turns or at the body cap, whichever first, and says `next` for the turn to continue from; a page anchored at its end (`from=last`, or `before=turn` for the page ending before a turn the client holds) fills backward from the anchor, so it always reaches it and `from` is wherever it filled up. The client opens on the tail and walks back with `before`, so a transcript whose turns are large never shows a stale end or a gap; a change is followed from the last turn held page after page until `next` is empty, up to ten pages. A page carries only the first 512 bytes of each tool call's input and result and of each activity's text, marked `more`, which is what keeps a turn with a hundred tool calls to tens of kilobytes rather than hundreds; `session.turn` reads one turn whole, at the conversation's revision, and the client asks for it when a turn's activity is opened. A single turn larger than 256 KiB is cut (final text kept whole where possible, activity text trimmed) and marked `truncated`. The page carries the `resume_id` it was read from: `/clear` and a discard rebind the record to a new transcript, and a client holding turn numbers from another handle drops them and refetches from 1. The last turn is always in progress until a `Stop` event: on a `changed {conversation}` the client refetches from the last turn it holds and **replaces** that turn and everything after it. A handle rebind (`resume_id` moved on the session view) changes the conversation cache's key, which emits `changed {conversation}` of its own, so the client needs no rule linking the two. Only Claude Code sessions have a conversation; Codex, shell, command and service sessions answer with a "no conversation" reason and the client falls back to `screen` (and, for commands and services, `run_output`).
- `session.last_response`: the last turn's `final_text`, its `n` and `end`. It is a **projection of the `conversation` key**: it is read from the same cache, carries the conversation's content revision, is watched by watching `conversation`, and refreshes on `changed {conversation}`; a window showing only the last response registers that watch. ## 5. Security and pairing

A local network is not a trust boundary: these APIs can instruct coding agents and expose private transcripts. The repo's rules apply unchanged: secret values never reach a record, a log line, a command line, or any reply but `env.resolve` (which is not on this port) and, as redacted text, the read models of §4.3; the Keychain holds key material.

- Require pairing **before** anything but `/info` and `/pair`.
- **Host identity**: a self-signed certificate made once with `rcgen` on first listen. The certificate is in `identity.json` (§3.1); its private key is a Keychain item through the existing adapter (`adapters/keychain.rs`, service `com.sadburger.switchboard`) under the account `remote-key:<server_id>`, so two data directories under one macOS account never overwrite each other's keys. The bundle must be signed with the stable identity (`scripts/bundle.sh`) or the Keychain ACL is lost on every rebuild.
- **What the client pins** is the SPKI SHA-256 of the host's public key, not the certificate's bytes, so a certificate reissued from the same key (a new expiry) still verifies. Rotating the key is making a new identity: every pairing is invalid and the dialog says so.
- **Pairing verifies the key before the code is sent.** The code alone would let an intermediary terminate the first connection, forward the code to the real host, and take the token. So the pairing window shows a **QR code** carrying `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`, and under it the same in text: a short form of the key hash and the code. The client scans or types both; it connects, compares the hash of the key it is actually talking to with the one it was given, and only when they match sends `/pair {code, device_name, spki_sha256}`. A client without a camera (visionOS gives an app none) pairs from the host's Bonjour record instead: it resolves the record, reads `/info` under no trust, shows the key the host presented in the dialog's short form for the owner to compare by eye, and pins that key for the pairing, so the typed code reaches only the host whose key the owner checked; a substituted certificate shows its own key on the device, where the owner sees it differ. The host refuses a pairing whose `spki_sha256` is not its own, so a relayed request through a substituted certificate fails even if the code reached it. Before pairing, `/info` is served to any client and nothing in it is trusted; after pairing, every connection verifies the pin before the token is presented.
- The pairing window is opened from the settings menu as "Allow pairing for 5 minutes", the same shape as the environment setup window (`ENV_SETUP_WINDOW`, never saved). The dialog that opens it chooses the scope the pairing grants, `read` by default.
- **The code**: eight characters from the 32-character Crockford alphabet (no `I`, `L`, `O`, `U`), 40 bits, drawn from the OS random source (`getrandom`), made when the window opens and shown as the QR's `code` and in text. It is single-use: the first successful `/pair` consumes it and closes the window. **Failures count globally**: one counter in the app's state, bumped on the frame for every failed `/pair` from any connection, and the window closes at three. Concurrent attempts cannot each get three, because the frame answers them in arrival order against the one counter.
- **The token**: 32 bytes from the OS random source, base64url, 43 characters. It does not expire; the owner revokes. It is sent only as a bearer header over the pinned connection, never in a URL.
- `/pair` answers with the token and the granted scope. The host stores the device name, scope, created time, last-seen time and the token's SHA-256 in `<data dir>/devices.json` (atomic write, owner-readable); never the token. The client stores the token and the pinned key hash in its Keychain.
- **Scope changes** happen in the host's dialog: a device's scope can be raised to `control` or lowered to `read` there, taking effect on the device's next request. There is no scope request over the port.
- **Key rotation** (a missing key at listen, §3.1) **deletes every record in `devices.json`** when the new identity is made, so an old token stops working on the first request, and the dialog says the pairings are gone. A client seeing a new key for a known `server_id` shows "identity changed, pair again" and sends nothing, token included.
- Every later request carries the bearer token; the host answers with the device's scope. A Settings dialog (built the way the Environment dialog is) lists paired devices with scope, last seen, and Revoke, and states what redaction does and does not cover. Revocation removes the record, takes effect on the next request and closes the device's WebSocket.
- The client verifies the pin on every connection and on endpoint changes; a mismatch is shown as "identity changed, pair again" and never auto-merged.
- Validate input, cap request bodies at 64 KiB, cap `lines` on `screen` (the wire clamps to 200) and `run_output` (500), cap pages and bodies as §4.2 says, and keep tokens out of logs, URLs, Bonjour TXT records and crash reports. Refusals are logged by op and kind, never with content.
- Loopback-only without auth is acceptable **only inside the spike directory**. No milestone commit binds a non-loopback interface without pairing.

## 9. Remote access later

Every server is an authenticated endpoint; nothing assumes RFC1918 addresses or Bonjour. A future Tailscale or WireGuard route, a manual remote endpoint, or an outbound relay reuses the same protocol, token and pinned key. No relay in v1. The pin is bound to the installation's key, not to an address or a certificate's validity window, so a route change or a reissued certificate does not invalidate it.

### 4.1 Implementation

- **No Tokio.** The host is std threads and `mpsc`; the core is owned by `SwitchboardApp` and every state change is a dispatch on the frame thread. The remote port follows the `ControlSocket` shape: an accept thread per listener, one thread per connection, each request handed over a channel to the frame, answered by the same `serve` path in `app.rs` (`serve_pending` runs before every frame, hidden ones included), the reply sent back on the connection's channel. A second runtime inside an egui app buys nothing for a handful of connections.
- **The frame does core state only.** A metadata request (a view, a command) is answered on the frame as the control port is. A content request (conversation, screen, run output, file) takes two steps: the frame answers with the **handle and the redaction policy** (the transcript path and resume handle, the pane's host id, the run's log path, the file's root and relative path, plus the secret values to mask and the policy fingerprint), and one **content worker thread** does the read, the parse, the mask, the version check and the serialization from a queue of such requests (one at a time, so one large parse is in memory at once; Spike 22 measured 575 MB peak for the largest transcript), then sends one small action back to the frame to record the version it observed (§4.4), and the connection thread writes the reply. The watch poll (§4.4) runs through the same worker. A multi-megabyte transcript, a 768 KiB file or a slow Keychain call therefore costs the worker its time and the asking connection its wait, never a frame. The handle is read under the frame's authority, so a record removed or rebound between the two steps makes the worker's version action a no-op and the reply carries the handle it read from.
- **Bounds.** The port is one user's few devices, and the limits say so:
  - at most 16 connections in total and 4 unauthenticated ones; a further accept is closed at once. The 4 are a separate pool: an unauthenticated flood fills its own slots and never a paired client's;
  - `/pair` is answered at most six times a minute per listener and `/info` sixty; past that the connection thread answers 429 without reaching the frame;
  - a TLS handshake and the first request line each within 5 s, a request body within 10 s, a write within 10 s; a connection that misses a deadline is closed;
  - one request in flight per connection (HTTP/1.1, no pipelining);
  - the frame drains at most 8 remote requests per pass, in arrival order, the rest waiting on the channel; the channel is bounded at 64 and a full channel answers 503 from the connection thread without reaching the frame; a frame-side request is a view or a handle lookup and takes microseconds, so the count is the bound;

Every server is an authenticated endpoint; nothing assumes RFC1918 addresses or Bonjour. The pin is bound to the installation's key, not to an address or a certificate's validity window, so a route change or a reissued certificate does not invalidate it.

# Changelog

Every user-visible change goes under Unreleased as it lands.
`scripts/bump.sh` moves that section under the next version with the
date, and `scripts/release.sh` publishes that section as the release
notes. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com)
and the versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.4.1] - 2026-10-21

- Dispatch takes an issue once per project rather than once across the data directory, so a second project on the same repository can take an issue the first already holds.

## [0.4.0] - 2026-10-21

### Added

- Dispatch reports each ticket's tokens by model and agent time, per attempt, stage and ticket, in `dispatch report` and a Usage tab on the ticket page.

### Fixed

- The session page's token count counts each message once, not once per content block, skips Claude Code's synthetic messages, and names each model when a session used more than one.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-10-19

### Added

- A session can be opened from the headset: a plus button on the Sessions tab, or "New session in this project" on a listed session, opens a Claude Code, Codex or shell session in a project on any connected host paired under the control scope, in the project's root or a directory under it, with a first message for an agent; the new session's window opens on the reply. The remote port takes `POST projects/{id}/sessions` for it and lists `create` among its capabilities.
- The remote port serves Dispatch's tickets: a listing with each ticket's standing and decisions, one ticket with its body, attempts and lanes, and under the control scope a decision answered or a parked ticket resumed. The headset gets a Tickets tab on it.
- The headset reads what each stage produced: every attempt lists its notes and other artifacts, its checks log, its review rounds' findings and responses and its evidence, each opened with a tap as text or as a picture; a ticket's timeline is read from the runner's event log; and a closable ticket can be closed. The ticket list is ordered last moved first, with a menu for the order (waiting first, newest, by project), the hosts, projects and states (closed hidden unless asked) and a "waiting on me" switch.

### Changed

- The headset's conversation view follows the end as a mode: it is held at the end, nothing growing under it can leave it behind, and a button at the right edge releases it for reading; the ellipsis at the foot returns it to following. Before, a new turn that began with a tool call could push the end off screen and switch following off, and the view could jump up to the turn it last held at the top.

### Fixed

- The headset's filter menu no longer jumps back to its top every couple of seconds while open: it is rebuilt only when a host or a session state it lists changes, not on every refresh.

# Plan: a web control surface on the remote port (#230)

The host serves a small page from the remote port's own listener. A phone
opens it from the pairing window's QR, pairs, lists the sessions with the
waiting ones first, reads a session's last response or screen, and sends a
reply. The page speaks the protocol the headset speaks. One commit; the app
runs at every step.

Line numbers are from this worktree at 7fe8949 (Release 0.4.1). "Facts"
means `facts.md` for this ticket; a decision that rests on its Settled
section cites the line, and one that rests on Unresolved or For the owner
says so where it is made and names the fallback.

## Where this departs from the issue

1. **The pairing values go in the URL fragment, not the query.** The issue
   writes `/?code=…&key=…&id=…`. `read_request` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:444`)
   splits the query off and hands it to the frame, and the browser puts the
   whole request line in its history and, by the issue's own account, sends
   the code to the host before `replaceState` runs. A fragment is never sent,
   never in a `Referer`, and not fetched by a link previewer. Whether the iOS
   camera or a previewer fetches the URL is Unresolved in Facts; the fragment
   is right whichever way that goes. The page and both native parsers accept
   either form, so the issue's URL still works. The shape is
   `https://<ip>:<port>/#code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
2. **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" stays true for everything but
   three files.** `serve_remote` refuses at `src/app.rs:3023`. The plan does
   not touch that line: the three page paths are answered on the connection
   thread before a request reaches the frame (Signals, below), so the frame's
   allowlist is unchanged and `/other` still answers the JSON 404 that
   `tests/remote.rs:464` asserts.
3. **The card's one-line excerpt is not on the wire, and the spec line that
   says it is does not match the tree.** `docs/remote-client.md` §4.3 (the
   `session.last_response` paragraph) says the excerpt "is `last_message` from
   the `Stop` hook on the record, a field of the session's metadata, and moves
   with `changed {session}`". `last_message` is carried by the hook event
   (`src/ports/events.rs:24`, `src/adapters/hooks.rs:71`) and nothing in
   `src/core` keeps it; `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637`) has no such
   field. The card's text is `agent_excerpt` (`src/ui/cards.rs:558`) over a
   parsed conversation, and a shell's is a `UiState` caption. This is also
   For the owner in Facts ("Excerpt on the wire"), unanswered. **Plan:** no
   new field. The page shows the state word and `waiting_reason` for every
   row, and for a Claude Code session the first line of
   `GET /sessions/{id}/last-response` (`text`, `src/content.rs:827`), fetched
   lazily for rows on screen, two at a time, because a read goes through the
   one content worker and enters the watch set (cap 128, `WATCH_CAP`
   `src/content.rs:42`). A shell, command or service row has state only. If
   the owner answers yes to an additive `SessionView` excerpt, the
   implementer moves `agent_excerpt` to the core, adds
   `#[serde(default)] excerpt: Option<String>` to `SessionView`, and the page
   reads it instead of fetching; nothing else in this plan changes. The
   commit also corrects the §4.3 sentence.
4. **A page needs to learn its scope later, and there is no way to.** Facts
   (Unresolved, last line) allows remembering the `/pair` reply's scope. That
   goes stale in the direction the owner most wants (raising a phone to
   `control` in the dialog, which §5 says takes effect "on the device's next
   request"). **Plan:** one additive authenticated read, `GET /api/v1/me` →
   `{device_id, name, scope}`. It is also the page's boot probe: a 401 from it
   is how the page learns it was revoked.
5. **"The page says so on its next request" cannot tell revoked from
   removed.** `authenticate` (`src/app.rs:3127`) answers the same 401 for a
   revoked token and an unknown one, and a rotated key also deletes the
   devices (§5). The page distinguishes by what it holds: a stored token
   getting 401 with an unchanged key says "this device was revoked or removed
   on the host; pair again"; a changed key says "identity changed, pair
   again" and sends nothing, token included (§5).
6. **§5 says "Require pairing before anything but `/info` and `/pair`" and
   the pairing hover says "only paired devices get past /info"**
   (`src/ui/remote.rs:~112`). Both change to name the three page files.
7. **The pairing window hands a phone an address that does not answer when
   the port is loopback-only.** Facts (Settled, `cx.remote_port` line) says the
   plan should close this. The QR's address comes from `local_address()` even
   when `identity.listen.lan` is false. The plan puts `127.0.0.1` in the URL
   in that case and the dialog says why a phone cannot use it (UI).

## The record

No new record and no `SCHEMA_VERSION` change (`src/core/model.rs:12`, 16
today; `VIEWS_SCHEMA_VERSION` `:612`, 7 today). A browser is a `PairedDevice`
(`src/ports/remote.rs:96`) like any other, named by the page in
`device_name`, which `remote_pair` already reads (`src/app.rs:3606`). The
page derives the name from `navigator.userAgent` (`Safari on iPhone`,
`Chrome on Android`, `Safari on Mac` for an iPad, which reports a Mac:
Unresolved in Facts, the For-the-owner question on naming stands). It shows
the name in an editable field before the code is sent, so the owner can type
"Sully's iPad". No `User-Agent` is kept by the host and `PairedDevice` gains
nothing.

**The certificate does change, and `identity.json` with it.** This is the
one place the browser surface touches stored state.

- *Why.* Facts (Settled, Apple row) says Apple wants the name in a SAN,
  `serverAuth`, and 825 days or fewer, and that the current certificate fails
  all three (`make_identity` `src/adapters/remote.rs:95–108` builds
  `CertificateParams::new(Vec::new())` with a CN only; not_after year 4096).
  Whether Safari then still offers "Visit this website" is Unresolved and
  needs a device.
- *Decision 1 (click-through or download), which is For the owner.* The plan
  builds **click-through as the trust step**, said in the dialog, with the
  certificate made acceptable to the browsers that check. It does not build a
  download route. Why: a download needs an iOS profile-install flow that
  Facts lists as Unresolved and must be tried on a device first, and it adds
  a route outside the three-file set. What click-through buys: the browser
  accepts this certificate for this address on this device, and the `key` in
  the URL lets the genuine page refuse to send the code to a host whose
  `/info` differs. What it does not buy: a page served by an impostor is not a
  genuine page, so the page's key comparison protects only against a host
  that differs from the one the QR named *and says so*; the dialog states
  that the trust step is the owner scanning the QR from their own screen.
  **Fallback if the owner wants a download:** add `GET /cert.der`
  (`application/x-x509-ca-cert`, the DER from `certificate_der`) to the
  static set below, and put the install steps in the dialog; the SAN reissue
  in this section still applies, since iOS wants the same fields.
- *What is built.* `make_identity` and a new `reissue_certificate(identity,
  key_pem, addresses, now)` share one parameter builder: SAN of each address
  given plus `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and `localhost`; `serverAuth` EKU;
  not_before `now`, not_after `now` + 800 days (`time`, already in
  `Cargo.lock` through `rcgen`, becomes a direct dependency; `now` is a
  parameter so the function is deterministic). The reissue reuses the same
  key from the Keychain, so `spki_sha256` is unchanged and every pairing
  stays valid: §5 pins the key and the `Pin` verifier
  (`src/adapters/remote.rs:183–197`) looks at nothing else.
- *`Identity` (`src/ports/remote.rs:25`) gains* `#[serde(default)] pub sans:
  Vec<String>` (the addresses the certificate names) and `#[serde(default)]
  pub certificate_issued: Option<SystemTime>`. `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION`
  (`:17`, 1 today) becomes the value in that file at implementation time,
  plus one: a ticket landing in parallel may take the next number first. An
  older file loads with both empty. `RemoteFiles::load` is plain serde, so
  no migration step is needed.
- *When it runs.* In `load_identity` (`src/app.rs:2781`), after the key check
  succeeds and not when `read_only()`: reissue when `sans` is empty, when
  `local_address()` is set and not in `sans`, or when `certificate_issued` is
  over 700 days old; then save the identity as `make_identity` does. A
  reissue never touches `devices.json`. A LAN address that changes while the
  app runs is not caught until the next launch; the dialog says so (UI) via a
  new `Identity::covers(ip) -> bool`.

## The signals

No new core signal, `AppAction` or event. The page consumes the existing
`/api/v1/events` socket (`hello`, `changed`, `removed`, `resync_required`,
§4.4) and sends `watch`/`unwatch` for the open session's `screen` or
`conversation` key. What is new is on the wire into the host:

**Static paths, answered on the connection thread** (`connection`,
`src/adapters/remote.rs:770`, after the rate check and before
`shared.requests.try_send`). They are constants and decide nothing, which
CLAUDE.md puts in the adapter; the cookie route would have needed frame state
(`Set-Cookie` after `/pair`), the route chosen below does not.

| Path | Content-Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /` | `text/html; charset=utf-8` | `web/index.html` |
| `GET /app.js` | `text/javascript; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.js` |
| `GET /app.css` | `text/css; charset=utf-8` | `web/app.css` |

The query and fragment do not matter (`read_request` already splits the
query; the fragment never arrives). Any other method on these paths is
`405` JSON; every other path keeps today's route to the frame and its JSON
404. A new `src/adapters/web.rs` holds the table (`include_str!` of `web/`,
the first text assets in the tree; `include_bytes!` is used only at
`src/main.rs:167` and `src/ui/theme.rs:203`) and the header set; `respond`
(`:530`) gains a sibling `respond_page(w, content_type, body)` that writes:

- `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src
  'self'; connect-src 'self' wss:; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action
  'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. Facts (Settled, CSP line) says `'self'` does
  not cover `wss:` in all browsers and the plan names it. It names the scheme,
  not the origin, because the address is not known to the binary and the
  `Host` header is not kept; the cost is that script that was already running
  could open a `wss:` connection elsewhere, which `script-src 'self'` plus
  text-only rendering (Tests) is there to prevent.
- `Cache-Control: no-store` (no caching across versions),
  `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. Facts
  (Unresolved, last-but-one line) says these are standard practice with no
  primary source fetched; adopted as such.
- `Connection: keep-alive` and `Content-Length`, as `respond`.

**Pool and rate.** Facts (Settled, `Limits::limited` line): a page load
counts against no rate window and only the 4-slot unauthenticated pool. The
plan adds a window, `PAGE_PER_MINUTE = 120` per listener (about 40 loads
with `no-store`), in `Limits` (`:621`) and `limited` (`:631`) for the three
paths, answering the existing 429. The unauthenticated pool is unchanged at
4 (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED`, `:567`): a connection that has only fetched files
is "unauthenticated" until a paired request, then moves to the paired pool
like any other. Whether a phone's parallel page load fits in 4 within the
30 s `IDLE_TIMEOUT` is Unresolved in Facts and needs a phone. **If it starves**
the implementer does not raise the pool; they set `Connection: close` on
the three file replies, which frees the slot as soon as the file is sent.
The page is three requests plus `/info`, `/pair` and `/me` and then one
WebSocket.

**Without a code and without a token**, the page loads and shows: the host
cannot be known, "Open the pairing window on the Mac (Settings, Remote
devices, Allow pairing for 5 minutes) and scan its code with this device's
camera." No fields to type a code into.

**Decision 2: the token reaches the WebSocket as a subprotocol value.** For
the owner in Facts, so the choice and its fallback:

- *Chosen.* `new WebSocket(url, ["switchboard.v1", "bearer." + token])`. In
  `read_request`, for an upgrade request with no `Authorization` header, a
  `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` list containing `switchboard.v1` and an entry
  `bearer.<token>` (token characters `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, at most 64) sets
  `bearer`; `authenticate` is unchanged. The 101 (`respond_upgrade` `:519`)
  echoes `switchboard.v1` only, never the token. Facts (Settled, RFC 6455
  block) requires exactly this: the server must echo one offered value or the
  browser fails the connection; base64url tokens are valid token characters.
  `RemoteRequest` gains `subprotocol: Option<String>` (the echo); the only
  construction site is `read_request` at `:506` (Facts, Settled, `RemoteReply`
  line), so no literal elsewhere breaks.
- *Why not the cookie.* A cookie is ambient: the browser attaches it to any
  request to that origin, so authentication stops being a header a
  cross-site page cannot send, and Facts (Settled, cookie block) says
  `SameSite` ignores the port, so another service on the same IP is
  same-site. That needs `Set-Cookie` on `RemoteReply`, a `Cookie` field, and
  an `Origin` check on every `POST` and the upgrade. The subprotocol keeps
  today's property that nothing authenticates unless the page's own script
  puts the token there. The Origin check on the upgrade stays optional per
  Facts and is not added. Whether a `Secure` cookie survives a click-through
  certificate is Unresolved in Facts; the chosen route does not depend on it.
- *Where the token lives.* `localStorage` under the page's origin, readable by
  script on that origin. The mitigation is the CSP above and a page that never
  assigns `innerHTML`.
- *Fallback if the owner prefers the cookie.* `RemoteReply` gains
  `set_cookie: Option<String>` written by `respond`; `read_request` keeps
  `cookie`; `authenticate` reads it when there is no bearer; `remote_pair`
  sets `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1/` and the page drops
  `localStorage` for the token; `RemoteRequest` keeps `origin` and the frame
  refuses a `POST` or upgrade whose `Origin` is not the request's own host.
  The `/me` probe and everything else stay.

**The page's pairing steps** (`web/app.js`), in this order and nothing
before step 1:

1. Read `location.hash` (and `location.search`), then `history.replaceState(
   null, "", location.pathname)`. Whether that keeps the code out of Safari's
   history and recents is Unresolved in Facts and needs a phone; the fragment
   choice (departure 1) is what makes the answer matter less.
2. `GET /api/v1/info`; refuse and say so unless `body.spki_sha256` equals
   `key` (case-insensitive) and `body.server_id` equals `id`. The page cannot
   see the certificate, only what `/info` claims (the issue's own caveat).
3. `POST /api/v1/pair {code, spki_sha256: key, device_name}`. A `403
   wrong_key`/`wrong_code`/`pairing_closed` is shown as that.
4. Store `{token, scope, server_id, key}` in `localStorage`, then `GET /me`
   for the live scope and start the session list.

Later visits: `/info` first; a key differing from the stored one →
"identity changed, pair again" and nothing is sent; otherwise `/me`; 401 →
"revoked or removed"; a network error → "can't reach the host" with a
retry. The events socket reconnects with a backoff of 1 s doubling to 30 s,
reruns `/me` (this is how a revoke, which closes the socket from the host
side in `dispatch_inner` `src/app.rs:486`, shows), and refetches on a new
`epoch` or `resync_required`, as §4.4 and the Swift client do. The page
orders rows waiting first (`/waiting`) within a project (`/projects`,
`/projects/{id}/sessions`), shows `card`, `waiting_reason` and `kind`, and
for the open session reads `/last-response` (Claude Code) or
`/screen?lines=40` (anything else), watched by `watch` on the same key. The
reply box exists only when `/me` says `control`; it posts `{op, text}` to
`/sessions/{id}/send` with `op` from `crypto.getRandomValues` (op is the
idempotency key, `src/app.rs:3159`), and a `403 scope` hides the box again.

None in `AppAction`/`Effect`. Frame-side additions in `src/app.rs`:

Core-side, one pure function: `invite_url(ip: IpAddr, port: u16, server_id:
Uuid, spki_sha256: &str, code: &str) -> String` in `src/core/remote.rs`,

Only `src/ui/remote.rs`, and the page itself.

The page, `web/index.html`, `web/app.js`, `web/app.css`: no framework, no

## The tests

No JavaScript runs in this tree's tests, and the plan adds no JS test tooling
(the issue: no dependency for the page). The page's JavaScript is therefore
covered by static checks plus the end-to-end flow driven from the host's
side, and the owner's phone run is the only check of the page's behavior.
The README and design status say so.

`tests/remote.rs` (a new helper beside `http()` `:245` that returns response

## Commit

`Serve a web control surface from the remote port, paired from a URL in the QR code`
